n88e2daa7c1f.s: With Mangalyaan (2014), India became which country in the world to reach Mars orbit?
n88e2daa7c1f.x: Mangalyaan reached Mars orbit on its maiden attempt, the first Asian mission, making India the fourth country to do so, not the third.

n69073a484b2.s: NSIL, the commercial arm of the Indian space sector, was established in:
n69073a484b2.x: NSIL was established in 2019; 1972 is the year ISRO came under the Department of Space.

nd5b886ec1e5.s: IN-SPACe, set up in 2020 as an autonomous single-window space regulator, is headquartered at:
nd5b886ec1e5.x: IN-SPACe, the single-window regulator set up in 2020, has its headquarters at Ahmedabad.

n3533f6430ec.s: The Indian Institute of Space Science and Technology (IIST) is located at:
n3533f6430ec.x: IIST is at Thiruvananthapuram; Gadanki hosts NARL, Mohali the SCL and Shillong the NE-SAC.

n49bdc0e40f6.s: Which ISRO centre handles satellite design and building?
n49bdc0e40f6.x: URSC designs and builds satellites; VSSC handles launch-vehicle design and development.

n00fc3dc41d7.s: In which of the following fields does the Indian Institute of Remote Sensing (IIRS), Dehradun offer training?
n00fc3dc41d7.x: IIRS trains in remote sensing, photogrammetry, cartography and geo-informatics/GIS; angiography and the other options are medical techniques.

n98150d90321.s: The Next Generation Launch Vehicle (NGLV) is meant to support India's crewed lunar landing goal by:
n98150d90321.x: NGLV is linked to the crewed lunar landing by 2040, not 2030; 2035 is the target for the Bharatiya Antariksh Station.

n2700cedab58.s: Which of the following is NOT correct about India's cryogenic engine development?
o: Early GSLVs used Russian cryogenic engines.
Cryogenic technology transfer was denied to India in the 1990s.
India's own cryogenic engine first succeeded on GSLV-D1 in 2001.
GSLV-D5 (2014) was the first success of the indigenous cryogenic engine.
n2700cedab58.x: The first successful flight of India's own cryogenic engine was on GSLV-D5 in 2014, not GSLV-D1.

n3dc0716360a.s: Which of the following is NOT correct about GISAT-1?
o: It was successfully placed in its intended orbit.
n3dc0716360a.x: GISAT-1 was lost because GSLV-F10 suffered a cryogenic-stage anomaly, so it never reached orbit.

new.s: The Indian National Committee for Space Research (INCOSPAR) was set up in:
new.x: INCOSPAR came first in 1962; ISRO replaced it in 1969 and the Department of Space came in 1972.

new.s: INCOSPAR, chaired by Vikram Sarabhai, functioned under the:
new.x: INCOSPAR was under the Department of Atomic Energy, not the Department of Space, which came only in 1972.

new.s: ISRO, which superseded INCOSPAR, was established on:
new.x: ISRO was formed on 15 August 1969 and superseded INCOSPAR (1962).

new.s:
Consider the following statements about the Department of Space:
1. It was created in 1972 along with the Space Commission.
2. ISRO was brought under it.
3. INCOSPAR was set up under it in 1962.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
new.x: DoS and the Space Commission came in 1972 and ISRO was brought under DoS; INCOSPAR was under the Department of Atomic Energy.

new.s: The first sounding rocket launched from Thumba on 21 November 1963 was the:
new.x: The American-built Nike-Apache was the first rocket from Thumba (1963); RH-75 (1967) was the first Indian-made sounding rocket.

new.s: TERLS at Thumba, Kerala, was chosen as a site because it lies close to the:
new.x: Thumba lies close to the magnetic equator, suited to the study of the equatorial electrojet.

new.s: With the launch of Rohini on SLV-3 in 1980, India became which nation to orbit a satellite with its own rocket?
new.x: Rohini (18 July 1980) on SLV-3 from Sriharikota made India the 6th nation to do so.

new.s: The Satellite Telecommunication Experiments Project (STEP, 1977-79) used which satellite?
new.x: STEP used the Franco-German Symphonie satellite; ATS-6 was used for SITE.

new.s: With SpaDeX docking on 16 January 2025, India became which country to achieve space docking?
new.x: India became the 4th country, after the US, Russia and China, to dock in space.

new.s: The heaviest payload launched from Indian soil, BlueBird Block-2 (6,100 kg), was carried by:
new.x: LVM3-M6 lifted BlueBird Block-2 on 24 December 2025, the heaviest payload from Indian soil.

new.s: Skyroot's Vikram-1 became the first privately developed Indian rocket to reach orbit in:
new.x: Vikram-1 reached orbit on 18 July 2026.

new.s: Who was ISRO Chairman (1972-84) when Aryabhata, Rohini and APPLE were launched?
new.x: Satish Dhawan headed ISRO from 1972 to 1984, the era of Aryabhata, SLV-3/Rohini and APPLE.

new.s: Mangalyaan (2014) was launched during the tenure of which ISRO Chairman?
new.x: K. Radhakrishnan (2009-14) led ISRO during Mangalyaan; Madhavan Nair led Chandrayaan-1.

new.s: Rakesh Sharma, the first Indian in space, flew in April 1984 aboard:
new.x: Rakesh Sharma flew on the Soviet Soyuz T-11 on 3 April 1984.

new.s: Megha-Tropiques (2011) and SARAL (2013) were satellites of India's space cooperation with:
new.x: Megha-Tropiques and SARAL, like APPLE on Ariane-1, are Indo-French cooperation milestones.

new.s: NISAR, launched in 2025, is a milestone of India's space cooperation with:
new.x: NISAR is an Indo-US mission, as was SITE with NASA in 1975-76.

new.s: The Indian Space Research Organisation (ISRO) was established on:
new.x: ISRO was formed on 15 August 1969, not in November; 1 June 1972 is when it came under DoS.

new.s: INCOSPAR, set up by Homi Bhabha in 1962, had whom as its Chairman?
new.x: Vikram Sarabhai chaired INCOSPAR, which Homi Bhabha set up in 1962.

new.s: The Department of Space works directly under the:
new.x: DoS works directly under the Prime Minister; ISRO is a constituent of DoS.

new.s: Dr V. Narayanan, ISRO Chairman from 14 January 2025, is the organisation's:
new.x: V. Narayanan is the 11th Chairman, succeeding S. Somanath (10th).

new.s: Who became ISRO Chairman on 15 January 2018, replacing A.S. Kiran Kumar?
new.x: K. Sivan, the 9th Chairman, served from 2018 to 2022.

new.s: Which of the following pairs (ISRO centre – person it is named after) is correctly matched?
new.x: URSC is named after U.R. Rao; SHAR honours Satish Dhawan and VSSC/TERLS honour Vikram Sarabhai.

new.s: India's first satellite Aryabhata and the SITE experiment were conceived by:
new.x: Vikram Sarabhai conceived Aryabhata and SITE; Satish Dhawan guided the programme through Aryabhata.

new.s: The National Remote Sensing Centre (NRSC), which receives and distributes satellite data, is located at:
new.x: NRSC is at Hyderabad; its forerunner was NRSA.

new.s: The Human Space Flight Centre (HSFC), Bengaluru, opened on 30 January 2019, mainly handles:
o: Gaganyaan mission planning and crew training
new.x: HSFC handles Gaganyaan mission planning and crew selection and training.

new.s: The Liquid Propulsion Systems Centre (LPSC) of ISRO is responsible for:
new.x: LPSC develops liquid and cryogenic stages; URSC builds satellites and SAC makes payloads.

new.s: The Indian Deep Space Network is located at:
new.x: The Indian Deep Space Network is at Byalalu near Bengaluru; Biak is an overseas ISTRAC station.

new.s: Under an ISRO-ESA Technical Implementing Plan, ESA provides ground-tracking support for:
new.x: The ISRO-ESA plan covers ground-tracking support for Gaganyaan.

new.s: The Third Launch Pad at Sriharikota, approved on 16 January 2025, is meant for:
new.x: The Third Launch Pad (Rs 3,984.86 crore, 48 months) is for NGLV; the first pad serves PSLV and SSLV.

new.s:
Consider the following statements about SDSC-SHAR, Sriharikota:
1. Its First Launch Pad serves PSLV and SSLV.
2. Its public Launch View Gallery opened in 2019.
3. It was renamed after Satish Dhawan in 2012.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
new.x: The First Launch Pad serves PSLV and SSLV and the gallery opened in 2019; SHAR was renamed after Dhawan in 2002, not 2012.

new.s: The Andhra Pradesh Space Applications Centre (APSAC) is located at:
new.x: APSAC, for remote sensing and GIS, is at Vijayawada; NARL is at Gadanki and NSTL at Visakhapatnam.

new.s: The Semi-Conductor Laboratory (SCL) at Mohali mainly works on:
o: Space applications for the North East
new.x: SCL Mohali does microelectronics/chip fabrication; PRL does planetary science and NARL atmospheric research.

new.s: CSSTEAP, the UN-affiliated centre hosted at IIRS Dehradun, was set up in:
new.x: CSSTEAP dates from 1995; IIRS began in 1966 and IIST in 2007.

new.s: ISRO's YUVIKA (Yuva Vigyani Karyakram), started in 2019, is a:
o: Young Scientist Programme for school students
new.x: YUVIKA is the Young Scientist Programme for school students; SPARK is the virtual museum and UNNATI the nanosatellite training.

new.s: How many Space Technology Cells (STC) has ISRO set up?
new.x: There are 9 Space Technology Cells, against 6 STICs and 6 Regional Academic Centres for Space.

new.s: Vikram-S ('Prarambh'), India's first private rocket launched on 18 November 2022, was built by:
new.x: Vikram-S was built by Skyroot of Hyderabad and was a suborbital flight.

new.s: Agnikul Cosmos' Agnibaan SOrTeD (30 May 2024) used which 3D-printed semi-cryogenic engine?
new.x: Agnibaan used the 3D-printed Agnilet semi-cryogenic engine; Kalam-250 is a Skyroot stage.

new.s:
Consider the following statements about Skyroot's rockets:
1. Vikram-S reached orbit in 2022.
2. Vikram-1 was the first privately developed Indian rocket to reach orbit.
3. The Kalam series are the solid stages of Vikram-1.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
new.x: Vikram-1 reached orbit in 2026 and uses the Kalam solid stages; Vikram-S was only suborbital.

new.s: The autonomous landing tests of ISRO's RLV-TD 'Pushpak' (RLV-LEX) were conducted at:
new.x: RLV-LEX landing tests (2023-24) were held at Chitradurga; they were landing, not engine, tests.

new.s: Which reusable rocket made the first orbital-class booster landing on 21 December 2015?
new.x: Falcon 9 made the first orbital-class booster landing; New Shepard is a suborbital reusable rocket.

new.s: The CE-20 cryogenic engine powers the:
new.x: CE-20 (LH2 + LOX) powers LVM3's C25 stage; CE-7.5 powers the GSLV Mk-II upper stage.

new.s: Aditya-L1 was launched on 2 September 2023 by:
new.x: Aditya-L1 flew on PSLV-C57 (XL); LVM3-M4 carried Chandrayaan-3.

new.s: PSLV-C48 (11 December 2019), the 50th PSLV flight, carried:
new.x: PSLV-C48 carried RISAT-2BR1 and 9 foreign satellites; Cartosat-3 flew on PSLV-C47.

new.s: GSAT-6A (March 2018), with which contact was lost after launch, was carried by:
new.x: GSAT-6A flew on GSLV-F08; GSLV-F10 carried GISAT-1.

new.s: The heaviest payload from Indian soil, BlueBird Block-2 (6,100 kg), was launched by:
new.x: LVM3-M6 lifted BlueBird Block-2 on 24 December 2025; the older record was INSAT-4CR on GSLV-F04.

new.s: SSLV is designed mainly for:
o: Low-cost, launch-on-demand launches of small satellites
new.x: SSLV is a low-cost, launch-on-demand vehicle for satellites of up to 500 kg to 500 km LEO.

new.s: The first SSLV flight, SSLV-D1 (August 2022):
o: Placed EOS-02 in its intended orbit
Was a suborbital test without a satellite
Failed to place EOS-02 in its intended orbit
new.x: SSLV-D1 failed to reach the intended orbit; SSLV-D2 (2023) and D3 (2024) succeeded.

new.s: SLV-3, India's first satellite launch vehicle, had:
o: Three solid stages and a VTM
new.x: SLV-3 had 4 all-solid stages; ASLV had 5 and SSLV has 3 solid stages plus a VTM.

new.s: PSLV can place about how much payload into Sun-synchronous orbit?
new.x: PSLV carries about 1,750 kg to SSO and about 1,425 kg to GTO.

new.s: The first successful flight of PSLV (D2, 15 October 1994) placed which satellite in orbit?
new.x: PSLV-D2 carried IRS-P2; Rohini RS-1 flew on SLV-3 and GSAT-1 on GSLV-D1.
